title: ROCm Optiq Memory Chart Layout (relational)
description: Data-driven description of the Compute kernel-details Memory Chart. The layout is relational: a set of block rows and a set of arrow (relation) rows, both keyed by id. This mirrors the shape stored in the compute_workload table. The interpreter (ComputeMemoryChartView) places blocks into columns, resolves each referenced metric against the compute metric table, and routes the arrows to avoid overlap.

metric_source.description: Which compute metric category/table the metric ids/names resolve against. Defaults to category 3, table 1 (the memory-chart table).

metricRef.description: A metric reference, as a string. Preferred form is the metric's canonical dotted id 'category.table.entry' (e.g. "3.1.0"), matching compute_metric_definition.metric_id. A display name (e.g. "L2 Rd") is also accepted as a convenience. The referenced metric supplies the value, unit, and - when no title override is given - the label.

contentItem.description: One line inside a block. Either a bare metric reference, or an object with an optional title override. The unit is taken from the metric entry automatically.

title.description: Label override; when omitted the metric's own name is used.

category.description: Semantic category driving the accent color. Recognized: read, write, atomic, util, hit, stall. Anything else (or 'misc') uses a neutral color. When omitted, the color is inferred from the label text.

id.description: Unique block id, referenced by arrows.

column.description: Column index (left to right). Blocks sharing a column stack vertically.

order.description: Optional sort key within the parent (column for top-level blocks, or the containing block); declaration order is used when omitted.

content.description: Metric rows shown inside a leaf block. May be empty for a label-only block (e.g. xGMI / GMI). Ignored when 'children' is present.

children.description: Nested blocks. A block with children is a container box (e.g. 'TCP' containing 'LDS' and 'GL0'); children stack vertically inside it. 'column' applies only to top-level blocks - children inherit their parent's column. Arrows still connect block-to-block by id, but a connection to a nested block terminates at its top-level ancestor's box edge, aligned with the block's row.

direction.description: Arrow head placement relative to (from -> to). 'forward' points at `to`, 'backward' points at `from`, 'both' is bidirectional.

title.description: Label override for the arrow; when omitted the metric's own name is used.
